subject: Edge relay consolidation & tenant boundary proposal — design review
messages:
From: Timothy Lowe <tim.lowe@edgeops.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: architecture@edgeops.io
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: consolidate tenant edge relays to a single fabric attachment

Jonas,

Thanks again for the intro call last week. As discussed, the EdgeOps team put together a short proposal for consolidating tenant edge relays for the Acme pilot into a single shared fabric attachment with host-level routing policies. The goal is to reduce cross-tenant NAT complexity and simplify observability while preserving per-tenant egress controls.

High-level items attached: controlplane-egress-diagram-v1.pdf and a small workbook (tenant-relay-proposal.xlsx) with traffic class estimates.

We'd like to run this by Redwood's control-plane/data-plane owners to validate assumptions about KV cache isolation, prefix routing, and fallback behaviors (canary fallback to per-tenant relay). Key questions for your review:
- Are we comfortable with a shared relay attachment that routes tenant egress through per-tenant VLAN tagging + ACLs?
- How would the Redwood runtime prefer to signal model-variant fallback to a different relay in case of congestion?
- Any major observability blindspots (tracing, token-level cost attribution) introduced by a shared relay?

Suggested time: 30–45 min sync today or tomorrow.

Thanks,
Tim
Timothy Lowe
Head of Architecture, EdgeOps


From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Lowe <tim.lowe@edgeops.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate tenant edge relays to a single fabric attachment

Tim — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. I skimmed the PDF and workbook; some initial thoughts below before we set a review:

1) Shared relay model: conceptually OK if strong isolation is enforced at the L2/L3 boundary (per-tenant VLANs + per-tenant ACLs), and we get deterministic egress SNAT mapping so billing/token attribution stays accurate.

2) KV cache and prefix isolation: this is the bigger concern. Our runtime assumes tenant request routing to a pinned backend instance for warm KV cache locality. If the relay homogenizes upstream endpoints, we need a way to preserve session affinity (sticky routing) back to a tenant-specific pool. Otherwise warm-start benefits degrade.

3) Fallback semantics: prefer an explicit routing tier flag in the request metadata (route_preference: primary_relay | fallback_relay) rather than implicit congestion probing from the runtime. That lets us do safe canaries and keeps the runtime's health checks simple.

4) Observability: request-level headers for tenant_id and route_preference will keep tracing and cost attribution intact. If the relay performs SNAT, include original-tenant headers before SNAT so our cost engine can ingest them.

Can we do a short design review at 2pm PT today? If that doesn't work, tomorrow 11am PT is fine. I'll add Marissa and Kimberly to cover ops & compliance angles.

Jonas Weber
Director, Deployment Architecture — Redwood Inference


From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Timothy Lowe <tim.lowe@edgeops.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate tenant edge relays to a single fabric attachment

Thanks, Jonas + Tim. A couple of compliance/operational notes from my side that should be in scope for the review:

- Audit trails: If the relay aggregates traffic, EdgeOps must provide an audit-stream (syslog or S3 delivery) broken down by tenant_id and egress IP mapping for SOC2 evidence. This is non-negotiable for regulated customers.

- Key management & IP hygiene: Per-tenant encryption keys for any edge-level secrets (TLS termination at the relay) must be surfaced to our KMS integration or handled in an HSM-backed key proxy.

- SLA/escape hatch: For Dedicated customers we often require a hard fallback to an isolated per-tenant relay if shared attachments impact P90 latency beyond agreed thresholds. Need to include automated detection + a rollout plan in the workbook (canary -> scale -> failover).

I attached two quick examples in the workbook tab — allocation thresholds and an escape-hatch playbook. Tim, can you confirm EdgeOps can emit the tenant-level audit stream and that the relay supports optional TLS pass-through?

Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Compliance Manager — Redwood Inference


From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, tim.lowe@edgeops.io
Date: 2027-08-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: consolidate tenant edge relays to a single fabric attachment

All — great thread. Quick recap and action items so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- EdgeOps proposes a shared fabric attachment with per-tenant VLAN tagging + ACLs, with session affinity preserved at the routing tier.
- Redwood needs: (a) tenant-level audit stream, (b) explicit route_preference metadata, (c) guarantee around preserving KV-cache locality or a defined fallback.
- Compliance ask: TLS pass-through option + KMS/HSM integration for edge-terminated keys, and an escape-hatch to per-tenant relays for Dedicated customers.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Tim/EdgeOps — confirm audit stream formats and TLS pass-through capability; provide a short matrix by EOD tomorrow. (owner: tim.lowe@edgeops.io)
2) EdgeOps — add route_preference header support to the request pipeline and document how SNAT will expose original tenant_id before detokenization. (owner: architecture@edgeops.io)
3) Jonas — draft a small runbook for canary -> scale -> failover including thresholds (P50/P90 triggers) and share by Friday. (owner: jonas.weber@redwood.com)
4) Kimberly/IRene — list compliance evidence required for a shared relay (audit logs, KMS proofs) and validate workbook items. (owners: kimberly.park@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com)
5) Marissa — sync with CS on how this impacts customer contracts and Dedicated SLAs; propose wording of an escape-hatch clause. (owner: marissa.cole@redwood.com)

Let's plan a 45-min technical review tomorrow 11am PT to go through a slightly expanded diagram set (Tim to attach a flow that highlights sticky routing). I'll circulate a calendar invite once Tim confirms.

Thanks,
Jonas
